Funded under the Cyber Funded Research programme, the project adopts a phased, rigorous approach running from January 2027 to December 2030. Over the initial two-year period, it will establish a comprehensive technology landscape of quantum sensing across all major modalities (electromagnetic, gravitational, inertial, timing, and hybrid): analysing the state of the art, monitoring global innovation trajectories, mapping technology supply chains, assessing ruggedisation prospects, and characterising the likely evolution of each sensor class towards the 2030 horizon. Building upon this foundation and a formal evaluation and benchmarking framework, the project will then transition toward down-selection: identifying the candidate quantum sensors that could realistically be tested between 2030 and 2032 and that will form the basis for later prototyping, demonstration, and field trials. All findings will be consolidated into a strategic research and development roadmap (2030-2040) guiding infrastructure investments, skills development, and partnerships, and positioning the Royal Military Academy as a national competence centre for quantum sensing.

MAIN TASKS:

• Establishment and yearly update of a structured technology survey of quantum-sensor platforms (NV centres in diamond, Rydberg atoms, atom interferometers, trapped ions, atomic clocks, superconducting circuits), including TRL and maturity assessment and a mapping of the global research and industrial ecosystem.
• Mapping of classical sensor technologies to contextualise potential quantum advantages.
• Identification and prioritisation of defence-relevant use cases through capability-gap analysis, cross-domain applicability studies, and workshops with engineering, physics, and defence-research experts.
• Definition of evaluation criteria and benchmarking frameworks combining scientific performance metrics (sensitivity, stability, bandwidth, dynamic range, coherence time), engineering integration factors (SWaP-C, environmental robustness, system complexity), and manufacturability and lifecycle considerations.
• Feasibility studies and maturation pathways: identification of technological bottlenecks, modelling and simulation of sensor performance in relevant conditions, and estimation of development timelines.
• Down-selection of candidate quantum sensors for prototyping and demonstration in the 2030-2032 window, validated through workshops with domain experts.
• Development of a strategic research and development roadmap (2030-2040) addressing infrastructure, skills and training, and partnership opportunities.
• Project management and coordination: planning, progress monitoring, annual reporting, and review meetings.
• Participation in NATO and EDA working groups on quantum sensors.
• Attending and presenting at international conferences
• Writing scientific papers and project deliverables (technology survey reports, use case catalogue, evaluation framework, down-selection report, strategic roadmap).

• Degree(s) required: PhD degree in a STEM field (Physics, Engineering Sciences, Applied Sciences, or a closely related discipline), preferably with a focus on quantum physics, photonics, or precision metrology.

• 
Ability to deliver high-quality scientific outputs relevant to engineering applications (peer-reviewed publications, technical reports).

jobs.occupation: PhD Researcher (M/F/X) Mathematics department > SMAC Unit Project: POSEIDON-NG M/W/X
jobs.description:
PROJECT:You will work within the SMAC Unit (Simulation, Modelling, and Analysis of Complex Systems) of the department of Mathematics of the RMA and in close collaboration with the Belgian and Dutch Navies. You will conduct scientific research at university level, leading to a PhD degree, on a project entitled POSEIDON-NG.The project aims to develop a next-generation, uncertainty-aware scheduling capability (computer implementation) to assess, plan, and optimise Mine Countermeasure (MCM) missions carried out by unmanned systems. Responding to Belgium's transition to standoff, drone-centric MCM operations under the Belgian-Dutch rMCM programme, the computer implementation must coordinate multiple unmanned surface, underwater, and aerial vehicles simultaneously, quantify and manage mission uncertainty (e.g., variable detection rates, timing variance, weather windows), generate efficient task sequences and routes, and adapt plans quickly as situational data evolves. The new POSEIDON-NG engine will serve as an advanced decision-support tool for the Belgian and Dutch Navies, providing reliable, conflict-free, risk-informed mission plans, rapid replanning, and operator-oriented features such as what-if (sensitivity) analysis and clear plan-quality indicators. The resulting capabilities will improve the planning, safety, tempo, and overall effectiveness of MCM operations and support the introduction of the new autonomous MCM fleet.

This work builds on prior RMA research funded by Belgian Defence. The DAP/22-14 project (SBOS for MCM) delivered the POSEIDON prototype, a two-level mission-planning engine: a low-level module computes detailed vehicle trajectories, sensor-informed detection performance, and the corresponding execution times, while a high-level module uses this information to schedule tasks, allocate vehicles, and coordinate routes across the entire mission using combinatorial optimisation based on Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP). The prototype also established graph-based shortest-path computation between mine zones, automated generation of mine-threat areas, and a practical operator interface to configure mission parameters and visualise plans. The proposed research will extend this foundation with uncertainty quantification, a bidirectional planning loop enabling rapid replanning, scalable optimisation methods (decomposition, heuristics, hybrid solvers), and exploratory quantum(-inspired) optimisation, transforming a promising prototype into an uncertainty-aware, scalable, and deployment-ready operational tool.

MAIN TASKS:Extension of the existing MILP-based scheduling formulation with uncertainty-aware constructs (robust, stochastic, or chance-constrained formulations).Development of a bidirectional coupling between the low-level trajectory and risk models and the high-level scheduler, enabling rapid mission replanning.Improvement of the scalability of the scheduling engine through MILP decomposition, heuristics and metaheuristics, and hybrid solver designs.Exploration of quantum and quantum-inspired optimisation methods (QUBO, QAOA, annealing-inspired heuristics) for selected combinatorial subproblems.Integration of all developments into the two-level POSEIDON-NG architecture and extension of the Graphical User Interface with operator-focused features (what-if analysis, plan-quality indicators).End-user engagement: definition and validation of representative MCM scenarios together with Belgian and Dutch Navy operators.Use best practices for code development and documentation.Attending and presenting at international conferencesWriting scientific papers and a PhD thesis.

About Us: Zymofix is a dynamic and innovative scale-up dedicated to fostering sustainable and circular agriculture. We specialize in creating effective and economically viable microbial products designed to reduce farmers' reliance on agrochemicals while maintaining high productivity. Positioned at the forefront of sustainable agriculture, we are committed to delivering cutting-edge solutions that empower farmers to grow healthy crops and improve yields without resorting to chemical fertilizers. Zymofix is planning the construction of an industrial-scale demonstration plant in 2027.
 

Job Description & Key ResponsibilitiesAs a OPEX engineer you will drive the continuous improvement culture within the production facility. In this role you will look beyond the surface, diving deep into the process to eliminate waste and scale manufacturing efficiency to the next level.
 

We’re looking for an energetic and enthusiastic personality with excellent communication skills, capable of inspiring and engaging teams to bring meaningful change and challenge the status quo, while respecting strict quality and safety.
 

Key Responsibilities
 
 

• Process Optimization: you are responsible for identifying, implementing, and ensuring process improvements to increase efficiency, quality, and safety. 

• Follow-up on KPI’s; apply value stream mapping and execute Gemba walks. 

• Based on data driven analysis, you identify hidden opportunities and propose improvements. 

• Lead independently cross functional improvement projects with minimal supervision. 

• Standardization & training: write, revise, and standardize Standard Operating Procedures to embed new best practices firmly into daily operations; deliver training modules to build a site-wide OPEX mindset. Responsible for keeping training matrix up-to-date and organizing training accordingly, in collaboration with the production team lead. 

• Identify root causes of technical anomalies/malfunctions or inefficiencies. 

• Provide support with day-to-day technical problems; act as a point of contact for problem solving. 

• Support implementation of new equipment, systems or workflows. 

The role requires strong analytical and problem-solving skills, preventive way of thinking, a high degree of independence, and the ability to collaborate effectively with a multidisciplinary team. 
 

You might be our perfect match if you meet the requirements below. But don't worry if you don't tick every box, we dare you to apply anyway. You never know if there’s another role at Zymofix that's a better fit for your skills.
 
 

• A master’s degree in engineering/biotech with a minimum of 3-5 years of experience in a continuous Improvement or OPEX role within a manufacturing environment; 

• Proven track record of applying operational excellence techniques as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping (VSM), and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in a production setting. 

• Analytical and data-driven, out-of-the-box thinking, solution-oriented mindset, and a hands-on approach. 

• Experience in biochemical process know-how and change-management is a plus. 

• A structured way of working, with an eye of detail, excellent communicator able to engage people, with a drive for continuous improvement. 

• Fluency in English, both verbal and written; fluency in Dutch is a plus.

jobs.occupation: Strategic Projects Lead - Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
About UsZymofix is a dynamic and innovative startup dedicated to fostering sustainable and circular agriculture. We specialize in creating effective and economically viable microbial products designed to reduce farmers' reliance on agrochemicals while maintaining high productivity. Positioned at the forefront of sustainable agriculture, we are committed to delivering cutting-edge solutions that empower farmers to grow healthy crops and improve yields without resorting to chemical fertilizers. Zymofix is planning the construction of an industrial-scale demonstration plant in 2027.
 

The RoleAs Strategic Projects Lead your core role will be to take ownership of projects that matter, from first idea to finished result. The job is mostly project-based. One project might be a market study for a new crop or region, the next might be designing the layout of our new offices or setting up our company OKRs. 
You will often get a question with little more than a goal attached. We trust you to figure out the rest: to structure the problem yourself and to deliver work of a high standard.
 

What You'll DoYour main focus is on strategic and operational projects. You will:
 
 

• Take full ownership of company-wide projects, from scoping and planning to execution and follow-up. 

• Conduct market research and analyses, for example on new markets, crops, competitors or customer 

• segments, and translate findings into clear recommendations. 

• Set up and follow up on our company OKRs together with management and team leads. 

• Handle confidential information, such as financial, strategic and personnel matters, with discretion.  

As Zymofix grows, new projects will land on your desk.

You might be our perfect match if you meet the requirements below. But don't worry if you don't tick every box, we dare you to apply anyway. You never know if there’s another role at Zymofix that's a better fit for your skills.
 
 

• You hold a master's degree in Bioscience Engineering (bio-ingenieur). 

• You are mature and discreet, and you know how to handle confidential information. 

• You set a high standard for the work you deliver: well thought out, structured and well presented. 

• You need few instructions to deliver a strong result. You structure a problem yourself, ask the right questions and take it from there. 

• You enjoy project work and are comfortable juggling several projects at once. 

• You have strong analytical skills and can turn research and data into clear, actionable conclusions. 

• You communicate fluently in Dutch and English, both spoken and written. 

• A first work experience, for example in consulting or a startup environment, is a plus.

As a production worker, you will work together with a colleague every day to manufacture safety boots 👢. You will place components such as the steel toe cap, lining and sole into the mould. The machine automatically injects the plastic, after which you remove the finished boot. In between production runs, you clean the machine to ensure it is ready for the next production cycle.

After training, you will also be able to operate other machines. You will cut away larger excess pieces and trim fine seams ✂️. You will carry out quality checks and pay close attention to detail. Every boot must meet strict quality standards. With your keen eye for detail, you make sure that only top-quality products leave the facility.

Working together with your colleagues is important. You step in where needed and support each other in achieving the production targets. You work accurately and take pride in the end result. Are you eager to learn and quality-focused? Then this could be the opportunity for you! ✅

Sound like the job for you? Apply now and discover how you can make a difference!

Who are we looking for?

• You have some initial stable experience in a production environment ⚙️
• You speak English well; Dutch is a plus.
• You have your own means of transportation (public transport is not available).
• You are attentive and have an eye for detail. 👀
• You can work at a fast pace and are physically fit. 💪
• You are not afraid of physically demanding work.
